key_insight: The mean polar-domain volume in imidazolium ionic liquids unifies two seemingly different transport trends—viscosity and ionic conductivity—into a common structure–property scaling law.
engineering_relevance: This descriptor offers a physically grounded way to screen and design ionic liquids with targeted flow and charge-transport behavior from molecular structure alone.
method: All-atom molecular dynamics simulations of imidazolium-based ionic liquids.
Compared transport properties across different anions and alkyl-chain lengths.
Correlated viscosity and ionic conductivity with mean polar-domain volume fraction using power-law scaling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative structure–property correlations across a chemically diverse set of ionic liquids, with both viscosity and ionic conductivity collapsing onto unified power-law trends versus polar-domain volume.
watch_item: The descriptor is validated on a specific imidazolium IL set, so broader generalization to other cation families or conditions will need additional testing.
paper_title: Polar-Domain Volume as a Unified Descriptor of Transport in Ionic Liquids
